subject: Cloud Computing
title: The SaaS Business Model
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The SaaS Business Model.

hook.text: Selling software used to mean one big sale per customer. SaaS turned it into recurring revenue forever.

buildup.text: Monthly subscriptions create predictable revenue. Investors love SaaS because cash flow is reliable.

discovery.text: The magic metric is 'net revenue retention': do existing customers spend more each year, or less?

twist.text: Great SaaS companies grow even if they stop acquiring new customers. Expansion revenue does the work.

climax.text: SaaS changed how software is built, sold, and valued. It created an entirely new business playbook.

punchline.text: SaaS isn't just technology. It's a business revolution.

quiz.question: Why do investors favor SaaS companies?
options: Recurring subscriptions create predictable, reliable revenue streams
SaaS companies never need to spend money on marketing
SaaS products are always profitable from day one

details.summary: The SaaS business model generates recurring revenue through subscriptions, with success measured by metrics like MRR, churn rate, and customer lifetime value. Low distribution costs and automatic updates make SaaS the dominant software business model.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding the SaaS business model explains vendor behavior: why free tiers exist, why companies aggressively pursue retention, and why pricing changes over time.
takeaways: Key metrics include MRR, churn, and customer lifetime value
Low distribution cost makes SaaS highly scalable

faq.question: Why do SaaS companies offer free tiers?
faq.answer: Free tiers acquire users at near-zero cost, creating a funnel where a percentage converts to paid plans. The strategy works because marginal cost per user is low and paid conversion rates of even 2 to 5 percent can be highly profitable at scale.

faq.question: What makes SaaS more profitable than traditional software?
faq.answer: Recurring revenue is more predictable than one-time license sales. Automatic updates reduce support costs for old versions. Cloud delivery eliminates physical distribution. These factors create higher margins and more predictable growth than traditional software.
